text:
marta: heads-up — customer-reported p95 jump right after the variant swap at 03:12 UTC, seeing p95 ~420ms vs baseline ~110ms. linking graphs: https://grafana.redwood/s/abc123
jay: deploy-bot shows canary roll at 03:12 to runtime v2.7.0-variantB
deploy-bot: rolled runtime v2.7.0-variantB to 10% canary (clusters: canary-3)
tanya: oncall evidence? any auth spikes or 429s?
marta: 429s flat, error rate unchanged. tail latency only. p99 spikes same timeframe — some requests hitting slow-paths.
leo: collecting flamegraphs and kernel selection traces now. I see an uptick in `sched_latency` for hotpath threads.
priya: this is from an enterprise customer — they've opened an escalation ticket, flagging user-facing latency.
support-bot: ticket #CS-7729 attached to thread
marta: quick stats from traces: before swap p95=112ms p99=320ms, after swap p95=420ms p99=1.2s. 99th looks worse but volume small.
jay: hypothesis: kernel selector or quant scheduler change in v2.7.0 causing some requests to take slow exec path. anyone run `vtable` diff?
leo: found an innocuous-looking scheduler tweak: `allow_late_binding=true` changed default in v2.7.0. Could increase contention for hot GPU cores under certain batch mixes.
tanya: can you reproduce on canary nodes with synthetic traffic that matches tenant cohort? we should run the same sample workload.
leo: running replay now against canary-3 with same tenant headers + warm KV cache.
leo: repro attempt 1: with warm-kv and identical mix — p95 ~130ms. repro attempt 2: cold-kv + peak concurrency — p95 ~410ms. so cold-kv + late_binding looks bad.
marta: customer reports cold-starty traffic pattern for a subset of routes (burst + idle). aligns.
jay: mitigation options: 1) disable allow_late_binding on canary, 2) pin hotpath to legacy scheduler, 3) temporarily route that tenant off canary. quick rollback vs targeted config tweak?
priya: customer prefers minimal disruption; routing off canary is OK short-term.
leo: config quick-fix: patch to set `allow_late_binding=false` in runtime config and roll to canary nodes. patch ready: `kubectl set env ds/runtime-config ALLOW_LATE_BINDING=false -n runtime` — will test.
leo: applied to canary-3, waiting 5m.
marta: graphs updating — p95 dropping to ~125ms on canary-3 after config flip :thumbsup: 
jay: ok that confirms hypothesis. next I'd like a bisect to find the exact commit that enabled the change (was default flip or a refactor?).
leo: commit range for scheduler changes: a1b2c3d..f7e8g9h. I'll run a binary search deploying intermediate builds to dev cluster.
marta: also let's draft rollback plan if wider rollout triggers. rollback steps:
- revert default in configmap (ALLOW_LATE_BINDING=false)
- scale canary to 0 traffic, promote stable v2.6.x
- notify customers
priya: ping me for the customer comms
jay: add tests: reproduce cold-kv + high burst scenario in CI perf harness and assert p95 < 200ms for target workloads.
leo: filed perf test: PERF-945, will attach replay script and sample headers.
marta: for now route affected customer off canary until v2.7.x is fixed. @infra please add traffic-split rule to route tenant=t-acme to stable pool.
infra-bot: traffic-split rule created: tenant=t-acme -> stable-pool
priya: thanks everyone — CS ticket updated with mitigation and ETA for fix.
leo: bisect notes: early results point to change in scheduler default layering, I'll post a short PR review and revert candidate this afternoon.
jay: follow-ups: 1) hotpath telemetry to detect similar cold-kv patterns automatically, 2) add canary gating: perf smoke on cold-kv scenarios before rollout.
tanya: if we need to rollback globally, follow rollback doc `docs/rollbacks/runtime-rollback.md` and notify #incidents.
marta: closing loop: will reopen if p95 climbs again. tagging thread in the customer ticket link.
priya: updated customer: temporary routing applied, we are working on patch and will provide ETA in 2-4 hours.
leo: attaching quick repro commands for the perf harness for reference:
```
# reproduce cold-kv burst
python replay.py --tenant t-acme --warm=false --concurrency 40 --duration 60 --seed 42
```
marta: thanks all, great quick turnaround :rocket:
